svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The nitrogen cycle: how nitrogen moves between the air, soil and living things."], [1, "Nitrogen fixation: bacteria in root nodules, lightning and the Haber process turn N\u2082 into compounds plants can use."], [4, "Plants absorb nitrate and make proteins; animals get nitrogen by eating."], [6.5, "Decomposers break down dead material and waste into ammonium (ammonification)."], [9, "Nitrification: Nitrosomonas turns ammonium into nitrite; Nitrobacter turns nitrite into nitrate."], [12, "Denitrification: in waterlogged soil without oxygen, bacteria return nitrogen to the air."]]
svg.title: The nitrogen cycle
svg.desc: The nitrogen cycle: nitrogen fixation, uptake by plants, feeding, ammonification by decomposers, nitrification to nitrite and nitrate, and denitrification back to nitrogen gas.
svg.text: Arrows: processes. Dots: nitrogen atoms moving along each one.

g.data-info: 78% of the air, but most organisms cannot use it directly: the triple bond is very strong.
g.text: Nitrogen gas N₂ in the air

g.data-info: Absorb nitrate (NO₃⁻) from the soil by active transport and use it to make amino acids, proteins and nucleic acids.
Get nitrogen compounds by eating plants or other animals; excrete urea.
Bacteria and fungi break down dead organisms, faeces and urea, releasing ammonium (NH₄⁺).
Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrite (Nitrosomonas) and nitrite to nitrate (Nitrobacter). They need oxygen: aerated soil.
N₂ is converted to ammonium/nitrate: by Rhizobium bacteria in the root nodules of legumes, by free-living bacteria (Azotobacter), by lightning, and industrially by the Haber process (fertilisers).
N₂ is converted to ammonium/nitrate: by Rhizobium bacteria in the root nodules of legumes, by free-living bacteria (Azotobacter), by lightning, and industrially by the Haber process (fertilisers).
Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrite (Nitrosomonas) and nitrite to nitrate (Nitrobacter). They need oxygen: aerated soil.
Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonium to nitrite (Nitrosomonas) and nitrite to nitrate (Nitrobacter). They need oxygen: aerated soil.
In waterlogged, anaerobic soil, denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas) turn nitrate back into nitrogen gas.
